blocks.content:
• Elastic rebound explains earthquakes.
• Largest earthquakes occur at convergent boundaries.
• S-waves cannot travel through liquids.
• Richter scale is logarithmic.
• Shallow earthquakes cause maximum damage.

items: Remember that S-waves cannot travel through liquids, which is crucial for understanding Earth's internal structure in exam questions.
Questions frequently test that shallow earthquakes, not deep ones, inflict the maximum damage.
Note that the Richter scale is logarithmic, meaning each whole number step represents a 10-fold increase in measured amplitude.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Elastic rebound theory provides the foundational explanation for how earthquakes occur.
The most massive earthquakes happen along convergent plate boundaries.
S-waves are strictly restricted from traveling through liquid media.
Magnitude on the Richter scale increases logarithmically rather than linearly.
Shallow-focus earthquakes are responsible for causing maximum surface damage.
